researched_by: the full text of the council's 2026 off-street parking order, the council's own motorhome and camping guidance, the district tourism board's car park directory, the cabinet report on the vehicle-nuisance PSPOs, and the landowners' own pages for the non-council car parks at Wells and Blakeney
policy_summary:
North Norfolk has NO overnight motorhome provision of any kind. Not one designated bay, not one aire, not one overnight tariff, no waste disposal point, no water. The council says so in terms: 'Overnight sleeping is not allowed in all of our Council car parks', and it is explicit that it 'does not provide facilities for servicing motorhomes, such as the provision of water, toilet emptying facilities or rubbish bins for domestic waste'. On a coast that draws as many vans as this one, that is the whole policy.

The instrument is the off-street parking order, not a PSPO. The North Norfolk District Council (Off-Street Parking Places) and Civil Enforcement Order 2026 came into effect on 7 April 2026 and revoked the 2025 order. Article 11(9)(a) prohibits using any part of a parking place, or any vehicle left in one, 'for sleeping or camping purposes'; 11(9)(b) adds eating or cooking. Article 11(13) bans erecting any tent, booth, stand or other structure - which catches a drive-away awning - and bans lighting fires. Article 11(14) bans entering a parking place while towing, which shuts out touring caravans altogether. Article 11(15) is the one people misread: a vehicle MAY be left stationed overnight, but only on purchase and display of an appropriate ticket, season ticket or permit. So the legal position is precise and it is not the one most van users assume. Parking an EMPTY motorhome overnight in a North Norfolk car park is lawful if you hold a valid 24-hour ticket. Sleeping in it is a contravention whatever ticket you hold.

There is a second, quieter exclusion. The schedule to the order admits 'all classes of vehicle except those exceeding a gross vehicle laden weight of 3.5t' at most car parks. A great many coachbuilt motorhomes are plated above 3,500kg. Those vehicles are not permitted in most of the estate at all, at any hour, whether or not anyone is asleep.

What the council DOES publish is a list of seven car parks where a motorhome physically fits and is welcome in the daytime: Cromer (Runton Road), East Runton (Beach Road), Happisburgh (Cart Gap), Mundesley (Gold Park), Overstrand (Paul's Lane), Sea Palling (Clink Lane) and Weybourne (Beach Road). These are mostly grassed coastal fields without marked bays, and the council's rule there is one ticket per vehicle; in town car parks with marked bays an over-long vehicle must buy a ticket for each bay it occupies. Note what is NOT on that list: Sheringham and Wells-next-the-Sea, two of the three places the register flags as pressure points.

Tariffs run in three bands - Standard, Resort and Coastal - from 60p for 30 minutes up to GBP11.50 for 24 hours at a Coastal car park, GBP46 for 7 days, charged 8am to 6pm from 7 April 2026. There is no motorhome tariff and no overnight tariff. Coaches have one; motorhomes do not.

CRITICAL OWNERSHIP POINT FOR WELLS AND BLAKENEY. The council's estate does not reach the two most sought-after stopping places on this coast. At Wells-next-the-Sea the beach car park and the town car park both belong to the HOLKHAM ESTATE, are locked at night, and prohibit coaches, caravans and trailers and any overnight parking; the Quayside car park belongs to the Port of Wells and bans campervans outright; the Freeman Street car park is run by Regional Car Parks and bans campervans and coaches. Only Stearmans Yard is the council's. At Blakeney all three car parks - Carnser (Quayside), Coronation and the Village Hall - belong to Blakeney Parish Council, with the National Trust as joint owner of the Carnser, and their published rule is that overnight camping in motorhomes or caravans is not permitted on any of them. No North Norfolk District Council decision can open any of these.

The district's only vehicle PSPOs, approved by cabinet on 3 February 2025 for Cromer, Fakenham, North Walsham and Stalham, are about car meets - revving, racing, doughnuts, amplified music - and include a prohibition on entering a public car park between 7pm and 6am for the purpose of vehicle display or racing. They do not prohibit camping or sleeping and they are not aimed at motorhomes.
notes:
This is the cleanest example in the dataset of an authority that has chosen restriction with NO paired provision. Compare Devon/East Devon at Exmouth, where the county pushed vans off the seafront and the district took them into car parks the same year; compare South Ayrshire, where the bays and the no-overnight signs went up together. North Norfolk has the prohibition and nothing on the other side of the ledger. The council's stated reasoning is not disorder but MARKET PROTECTION - its own guidance says the rule exists to protect residents' quality of life and to avoid unfair competition with the district's licensed campsites, and the district councillor quoted on the Salthouse restriction pointed motorhome users to 'registered and certified camping and caravan sites'. That is an unusually candid statement of why a council would decline to build an aire, and it is worth recording as such.

The instrument choice confirms a pattern now seen in half a dozen English districts: the off-street parking order, not the PSPO, is the tool of choice, and the drafting bites on SLEEPING rather than on parking. North Norfolk goes further than North Devon by adding 'camping' alongside 'sleeping' in the same sub-paragraph and by separately banning tents, structures and fires. Between them Articles 11(9), 11(13) and 11(14) close off every version of staying the night except sitting in a sealed, silent, unlit van - which is precisely what 11(9)(a) then prohibits.

A REAL CONTRADICTION TO FLAG. The district tourism board tells visitors the car parks 'are usually open 24 hours-a-day and are free from 6pm to 8am'. The order says no vehicle may be left stationed overnight without a valid ticket or permit. Both can be true - the TARIFF stops at 6pm while the requirement to hold a ticket to be there overnight does not - but the published messages point in opposite directions, and an unbriefed van reading the tourism page will conclude, wrongly, that a North Norfolk car park after 6pm is free and unregulated.

The 3.5-tonne class limit is the underrated finding. Nobody in the van community discusses it and no council page highlights it, but it is in the schedule to the order and it excludes a large slice of the coachbuilt motorhome fleet from most of the estate outright. It also means the seven 'motorhome-friendly' coastal car parks are, for a 3.9t van, not obviously available either - this needs checking site by site against the schedule.

WASTE IS THE DRIVER. Every strand of this policy - the council's guidance, the tourism board's page, the news coverage, and the county's Salthouse order twelve miles away - traces back to chemical toilet cassettes being emptied into public toilets, drains and roadside ditches. Anglian Water is publicly involved. North Norfolk's response has been to tell people not to do it while providing nowhere to do it properly. South Ayrshire faced the identical problem at Girvan harbour and built the facility instead; the two files read as a controlled experiment.

Direction of travel: static and hardening at the edges. The 2026 order carried the sleeping and camping prohibition forward unchanged from 2025 and added no motorhome provision; the county tightened one coastal road at Salthouse in 2025; the parish and estate landowners at Blakeney and Wells lock up at night. Nothing found suggests any part of this system is moving towards provision.
open_questions: Does the 3.5t gross laden weight class limit apply at the seven car parks the council itself lists as suitable for motorhomes? If it does, the council is simultaneously inviting motorhomes and excluding most of them. The schedule needs reading car park by car park.

Is the 'no sleeping or camping' condition signed on site, or does it live only in the order? The council says penalty notices 'can be' issued for overnight camping, which is not the same as saying they are.
How many PCNs has North Norfolk actually issued for overnight camping in a car park? No enforcement figures were found. Without them the prohibition may be nominal.

The two Wells-next-the-Sea entries in the 2026 order are Stearmans Yard and Staithe Street (12 spaces). Confirm there is no third council car park in Wells - the town has at least five car parks and four of them are not the council's.

Are the four vehicle-nuisance PSPOs actually in force, and from what date? Cabinet approved them on 3 February 2025 and local press reported a clampdown coming into force, but the making date and the three-year expiry could not be pinned down.

Sea Palling (Clink Road) is the largest car park in the estate at around 1,000 grassed spaces and is on the motorhome-suitable list. Local press reported a separate bid to ban parking on a road in Sea Palling all year round - a county highways matter, but it would displace vehicles into or out of this car park. Unresolved.

Is there any private or commercial motorhome stopover inside the district that fills the gap the council leaves? The council directs users to 25 registered campsites but no aire-style overnight facility was identified.

Whether Cromer Runton Road - 1,037 spaces, the largest coastal car park in the district and the one nearest the pressure - has ever been considered for an overnight scheme. No committee paper proposing one was found.

prohibits: sleeping or camping in a vehicle
excludes_vehicle_types: caravan (no towing into a parking place)
vehicles over 3500kg gross laden weight at most car parks
sites.notes: THE OPERATIVE RULE FOR THE WHOLE ESTATE. The North Norfolk District Council (Off-Street Parking Places) and Civil Enforcement Order 2026, in effect 7 April 2026, revoking the 2025 order. Article 11(9)(a): no person shall use any part of a parking place, or any vehicle left in a parking place, for sleeping or camping purposes; 11(9)(b) adds eating or cooking. Article 11(13) prohibits erecting any tent, booth, stand, building or other structure and lighting any fire. Article 11(14) prohibits entering a parking place while towing, which excludes touring caravans. Article 11(15) permits a vehicle to be left stationed overnight ONLY on purchase and display of an appropriate ticket, season ticket or permit. The distinction matters: an empty motorhome left overnight on a valid 24-hour ticket is lawful; sleeping in it is not, on any ticket. The schedule admits all classes of vehicle EXCEPT those over 3.5t gross laden weight at most sites, with coaches excluded at some - a separate and much less publicised bar on heavier motorhomes. Maximum stay is 7 days at most car parks, 24 hours at some. Enforced by penalty charge notice. Charging 8am to 6pm; no motorhome tariff and no overnight tariff exists anywhere in the estate.

sites.name: Runton Road Car Park, Cromer
sites.notes: The biggest car park in the district at about 1,037 spaces, on the clifftop west of Cromer pier, with toilets. It is ON the council's published list of car parks suitable for motorhomes - but that is a DAYTIME statement only. Coastal tariff band, charged 8am to 6pm, up to GBP11.50 for 24 hours. Article 11(9)(a) 'no sleeping or camping' applies here as everywhere else, and Cromer is additionally covered by one of the four vehicle-nuisance PSPOs. This is the obvious place an unbriefed van heads on the North Norfolk coast and it is the single most likely place in the district to be moved on.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of NR27 9AU, the postcode the council and the district tourism board publish for Runton Road car park on the Cromer clifftop

sites.name: Station Approach Car Park, Sheringham
sites.notes: The main Sheringham car park, about 294 spaces beside the North Norfolk Railway station, toilets nearby. SHERINGHAM IS NOT ON THE COUNCIL'S MOTORHOME-SUITABLE LIST - none of its six car parks is. This is a marked-bay town car park, so an over-long vehicle must buy a ticket for every bay it occupies, and the 3.5t class limit applies. Combined with Article 11(9)(a) there is no lawful way to stay the night in a vehicle anywhere in Sheringham on council land.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of NR26 8RG, the postcode published for Station Approach car park by Sheringham station

sites.name: Stearmans Yard Car Park, Wells-next-the-Sea
sites.notes: THE ONLY COUNCIL CAR PARK OF ANY SIZE IN WELLS - about 160 spaces with EV charging and toilets, charged 8am to 6pm. The council's other Wells entry, Staithe Street, has 12 spaces. Wells is NOT on the motorhome-suitable list. Every other car park in the town belongs to someone else and every one of them bans campervans or overnight parking outright: the beach and town car parks are Holkham Estate and are locked at night, the Quayside is the Port of Wells and prohibits campervans, and Freeman Street is Regional Car Parks and prohibits campervans and coaches. So in the busiest harbour town on this coast there is exactly one car park a motorhome may lawfully occupy at all, and Article 11(9)(a) prohibits sleeping in it.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of NR23 1BA, the postcode published for Stearmans Yard by both the council and the Wells visitor guide

sites.name: Beach Road / Gold Park Car Park, Mundesley
sites.search_hint: Gold Park car park, Beach Road, Mundesley
sites.notes: About 80 spaces with toilets, above Mundesley beach. ON the council's motorhome-suitable list, so a motorhome may park here in the daytime on a single ticket, but Article 11(9)(a) prohibits sleeping or camping and there is no overnight tariff. Resort or Coastal tariff band, charged 8am to 6pm.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of NR11 8BG, the postcode the council publishes for the Beach Road / Gold Park car park

sites.name: Paul's Lane Car Park, Overstrand
sites.notes: About 250 spaces on GRASS with toilets, just east of Cromer. ON the council's motorhome-suitable list and one of the coastal car parks with no marked bays, where the council's published rule is one ticket per vehicle however large it is. Comfortable to park in, unlawful to sleep in: Article 11(9)(a) applies and there is no overnight provision. The unmarked grass surface is exactly what makes these coastal fields attractive to vans and exactly why the council keeps having to restate the rule.

sites.name: Wells-next-the-Sea beach and town car parks (Holkham Estate)
sites.notes: NOT COUNCIL LAND - RECORDED SO THE MAP DOES NOT IMPLY COUNCIL CONTROL. The Beach Road car park at the end of the pinewoods (NR23 1DR) and the Wells Town car park (NR23 1FD) are both run by the HOLKHAM ESTATE, a private estate. Attendants are on duty, tariffs run to GBP14 for over four hours or all day, and the published rule for both is that coaches, caravans and trailers are prohibited and the car park is LOCKED AT NIGHT with no overnight parking permitted. Opening hours are seasonal - roughly 6am to 9pm in season. Nothing North Norfolk District Council does can open these; no overnight scheme can be extended to them. The two other non-council car parks in Wells are the Quayside, run by the Port of Wells, which prohibits overnight parking, campervans and motorcycles, and the Freeman Street car park run by Regional Car Parks, which prohibits campervans and coaches. Between them these four car parks close off the whole of Wells to an overnight van.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of NR23 1DR, the sat-nav postcode Holkham publishes for the Wells beach car park at the north end of Beach Road; the Wells Town car park is about three quarters of a mile south

sites.name: Blakeney car parks (Carnser/Quayside, Coronation, Village Hall)
sites.notes: NOT COUNCIL LAND EITHER. North Norfolk District Council has NO car park in Blakeney - the 2026 order's schedule does not list one. All three Blakeney car parks belong to Blakeney Parish Council: the Village Hall car park on Langham Road (free), the Coronation car park on the High Street (pay and display, GBP6 for 24 hours, 30 minutes free), and the Carnser (Quayside) car park, which the parish council owns and manages JOINTLY WITH THE NATIONAL TRUST and which is attended April to October. The parish council's published rule is unambiguous and covers all three: overnight camping in motorhomes, caravans or anything else is not permitted on any of its car parks. Enforcement is by landowner signage and attendants, not by penalty charge notice - a different legal route with different consequences. Coordinates are on the Carnser, the quayside car park a van would actually aim for.
sites.geocode_precision: OpenStreetMap way 177988715, Blakeney Carnser car park on the quay, which also records the joint National Trust and parish council operation

sites.name: Vehicle nuisance PSPOs - Cromer, Fakenham, North Walsham and Stalham
sites.notes: RECORDED SO NOBODY RESEARCHES IT TWICE: these PSPOs do NOT prohibit camping or sleeping in a vehicle. Four orders covering Cromer, Fakenham, North Walsham and Stalham, approved by cabinet on 3 February 2025 for three years, aimed squarely at car meets - excessive speed, repeated acceleration, racing, doughnuts, handbrake turns, burnouts, engine revving, horn use, amplified music and intimidating behaviour associated with a vehicle. The one limb that touches overnight use is a prohibition on entering a public car park between 7pm and 6am FOR THE PURPOSE OF vehicle display or racing; the purpose test means an overnight motorhome is not caught. Breach is a fixed penalty notice or, on summary conviction, a fine up to level 3. North Norfolk therefore relies entirely on its off-street parking order, not on a PSPO, for anything to do with sleeping in vehicles - the same choice made by North Devon and by most English districts in this dataset. The council's own PSPO page says the orders apply 'at all times and throughout the year', which sits oddly with the 7pm-6am car park limb in the cabinet report; the made orders should be read to settle it.
